fact_rationales.F12: Single S2 and systolic ejection murmur are more typical of truncus arteriosus due to the common arterial trunk, whereas tricuspid atresia would more likely present with different auscultation findings.
fact_rationales.F15: Enlarged cardiac silhouette with increased pulmonary vasculature is highly suggestive of truncus arteriosus due to the increased blood flow to the lungs, whereas tricuspid atresia might show different imaging characteristics due to the underdevelopment of the right ventricle and the presence of atrial septal defect or patent foramen ovale.

fact_rationales.F12: Single S2 and systolic ejection murmur are more typical of ventricular septal defects and atrioventricular septal defects, which often present with similar auscultation findings.
fact_rationales.F15: Enlarged cardiac silhouette with increased pulmonary vasculature is highly suggestive of a left-to-right shunt, which is most consistent with a ventricular septal defect.

why.B1.1: Hypoplastic Left Heart Syndrome is a strong candidate due to the underdeveloped left heart structures leading to a single S2, systolic ejection murmur, and the radiographic findings of an enlarged cardiac silhouette with increased pulmonary vasculature.
why.B2.1: Ventricular Septal Defect is a possible explanation for the observed findings, including the single S2, systolic ejection murmur, and the chest imaging findings, but it is less specific than Truncus arteriosus and Hypoplastic Left Heart Syndrome.
why.B4.4: Truncus arteriosus best explains the single S2, systolic ejection murmur, and enlarged cardiac silhouette with increased pulmonary vasculature due to the common arterial trunk and increased blood flow to the lungs.
